full_judgment:
6. During pendency of the Artha Rin case the petitioner-company filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the CPC read with section 57 of the Ain, 2003 for rejection of plaint mainly on the ground that the suit is barred by limitation as per provision of section 46 of the Ain, 2003. 

 10. Mr Shah Md Munir Sharif, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner-company in the course of argument after placing the writ petition along with annexures, submits that the Adalat under misconception of law and facts most illegally rejected the application under Order VII, rule 11 of the CPC read with section 57 of the Ain, 2003 ignoring the mandatory provision of section 46 of the Ain, 2003. Mr Munir Sharif next, on referring the provision of section 46 of the Ain, 2003, submits that as per mandatory provision of section 46(1)(ka) of the Ain, 2003, the plaintiff-bank must file the suit within 1(one) year if the borrower fails to repay the loan amount as per terms of the agreement but, in this case, it is evident from the plaint that the outstanding amount was over due on 17-9-2003 although the suit was filed on 9-6-2005 that is beyond one year and therefore, the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation and, as such, the impugned order is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 11. On the other hand, Mr ASM Abdur Razzaque, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 3, Uttara Bank Limited supports the impugned order which was, according to him, correct, just and proper. The learned Advocate, in the course of argument after placing the affidavit-in-opposition and other connected papers, submits that the grounds set forth in the writ petition are misconceived, vague, malafide and without any legal basis. The learned Advocate next, referring the provision of section 46 of the Ain, 2003, submits that a combined reading of the same clearly shows that if a suit is filed after expiry of the time limit as specified in sub-section (1) or (2) of the Ain, 2003, the Court shall immediately communicate the matter to Chief Executive of the concerned bank or financial institution in writing and if the suit has not been filed for negligence of any officer of the said financial organisation, the competent authority shall take penal action against the officer responsible for such fault and therefore, in such view of the matter, it cannot be said that if the financial institution could not file the suit against the borrower or borrower-company within time the suit will be barred by limitation. In elaborating his submission he has drawn our attention to the provision of section 46 of the Ain, 2003 and submits that on a reading of the sub-sections of section 46 of the Ain, 2003 shows that the provision of the said section is directory in nature and thus, in any view of the matter, the order dated 26-11-2006 (Annexure D) does not suffer from any legal infirmity, rather it is well founded in law. Mr Razzaque, to strengthen his submission, has relied on the decisions reported in 1989 BLD 304, AIR 1980 (SC) 303 and 11 DLR (SC) 200. 

 12. Mrs Sufia Ahammed, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the respondent No. 1, the Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, at the very outset takes us to the relevant provision of section 46 of the Ain, 2003 and then submits the same clearly indicates that if the financial institution did not file any suit within the specified period, the competent authority shall take disciplinary and penal action against the officer responsible for such lapse but there is nothing in the said section or in the Ain, 2003 that if the financial institution did not or could not file any suit within the specified time the suit will be barred by limitation. The learned Assistant Attorney-General further contends that the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is a special law and the Adalat was created thereunder to recover outstanding loans given by the banks or financial institutions by special method which would take lesser time than the normal process of realisation of loan. Besides, the provisions of section 46 of the Ain, 2003 is absolutely directory in nature and thus, in no way it can be said since the bank or financial institution has filed the suit beyond the specified time the plaint of the suit is liable to be rejected and hence the impugned order does not call for any interference by this Court. Mrs Sufia Ahmed in support of her last submission has relied on the cases reported in 1989 BLD 304, 1988 BLD 686, 11 DLR (SC) 200, 17 DLR 191 and 38 DLR (AD) 172. 

 মামলা দায়ের সম্পর্কিত বিশেষ বিধান ও সময়সীমা-The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act No. IX of 1908) এ ভিন্নতর বিধান যাহাই থাকুক না কেন, কোন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান সম্পাদিত চুক্তি বা চুক্তির শর্ত অনুযায়ী ঋণ গ্রহীতার নিকট হইতে ঋণ পরিশোধ সূচি (Repayment schedule) অনুযায়ী ঋণ পরিশোধ শুরু হইবার পরবর্তী- 

 14. A reading of the these sub-sections together and as a whole, indicates that if a borrower fails to pay back the loan according to terms of agreement, the bank or financial organisation will file a suit within one year and if the suit is filed after expiry of the time limit as specified in sub-sections (1) and (2) to section 46 of the Ain, 2003 the Court shall immediately communicate the matter to Chief Executive of the concerned financial institution in writing and if the suit has not been filed for negligence of any officer of the said financial organisation, the competent authority shall take penal and disciplinary action against the officer responsible for such fault or negligence. It therefore, seems clear that if the suit is filed by the Bank or financial institution after expiry of the time limit as specified in sub-sections (1) and (2) as may be applicable the Court shall immediately communicate the matter to Chief Executive of the concerned financial institution in writing and the competent authority of the concerned bank or financial institution shall take penal and disciplinary action against the officer responsible for such negligence. In view of this, we do not find any possible reason to agree with the contention as canvassed by Mr Shah Md Munir Sharif that the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation as per provision of section 46 of the Ain, 2003 on the ground that since the bank could not or did not file the suit within one year as per provisions of section 46 (1)(ka) of the Ain, 2003. 

 17. In this backdrop as well as the principles laid down in those cited decisions so far as it relates to the question whether the provision of the statute is mandatory or directory, our considered opinion is that the provision of section 46 of the Ain, 2003 so far it relates to the question of filing the suit by the bank or financial institution against the borrower within specified time is directory and not at all mandatory and therefore, in any view of the matter, the suit is not barred by limitation. Thus, we do not find any illegality or impropriety in the impugned order of the learned Judge of Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka. Hence, the Rule fails.
